title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Playbook for authoring, publishing, and operating Developer Experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts, templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and canonical fixes for top support issues.
content:
Overview

This document captures standards, workflows, and canonical content to operate Redwood Inference's developer-facing documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and canonical fixes for top support issues. Target readers: DevEx writers, SDK owners, support engineers, and on-call staff.

Goals
- Provide consistent, searchable, and runnable SDK guides and API examples that enable fast integration.
- Maintain canonical quickstarts and templates for common patterns (chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming).
- Ensure docs-site operations are repeatable and reduce live-site incidents.
- Surface top support issues with canonical reproductions and fixes to reduce time-to-resolution.

Scope
- SDKs: REST/HTTP, official TypeScript/Node, Python, and Go SDKs.
- Quickstarts & templates: single-file examples, repo templates, and deployment examples for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.
- API examples: request/response pairs, streaming examples, function/tool-calling examples, and error handling.
- Docs-site ops: publish workflow, rollout checklist, monitoring, and incident response.
- Support issues: top 12 support issues with root cause, reproduction steps, fix, and mitigation.

Ownership and Roles
- Primary owner: DevEx (eng-developer-experience)
- Reviewers: SDK owners (pkg-sdks), Support (customer-success), Security (security-and-compliance) for sensitive content
- Publishing: Docs site maintainer (docs-site team) for releases and redirects

Standards for Content Authoring
1) Tone & Style\- Use active voice; keep examples minimal and runnable.
- Assume reader is an engineer; prefer concrete examples and CLI snippets.
2) File and Page Naming\- Filenames should be short and descriptive with words connected by dashes, e.g. developer-sdk-quickstart-node-2026.json.
- Headings: H1 (title), H2 for major sections, H3 for substeps.
3) Metadata\- Every page must include: title, summary, author, owner_team, reviewers, status, created_at, last_updated, labels, related_pages, confidentiality.
4) Code and Examples\- Provide copy-pasteable snippets. Include minimal environment setup steps and expected output.

Content Types and Templates
- SDK Guide (Template)
  - Purpose: short (1-2 sentences)
  - Prerequisites: SDK version, credentials, environment variables
  - Quickstart: 5-10 line runnable example (authenticate, call, parse response)
  - Deep dive: pagination/streaming/advanced options, configuration reference table
  - Troubleshooting: 3 common errors and fixes
- Quickstart (One-pager)
  - Objective: example goal (e.g., \"Integrate chat with streaming responses\")
  - Steps: numbered minimal steps with CLI and code snippets
  - Expected result: example response or behavior
  - Next steps & links to templates and SDK guide
- Template Repository README
  - Purpose, license, supported runtimes, CI instructions, deployment notes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- API Example Page
  - Example name, HTTP request, sample response, streaming variant, error examples, and recommended retry/backoff behavior

Canonical Sections (required on each guide)
- Getting started (prereqs)
- Minimal example (copy/paste runnable)
- Reference (config table or flags)
- Troubleshooting & support links

Docs-site Operating Procedures (doc-site-ops)
1) Publish workflow
- Draft -> in_review -> published.
- Use PR templates: include a short changelog and test links (local build URL + staging URL).
- Staging promotion: smoke tests and a link to an automated build (CI artifact).
2) Rollout checklist (pre-publish)
- Verify metadata (title, labels, related_pages).
- Run local docs build: mkdocs or Hugo build success.
- Validate code snippets with snippet runner (CI job: docs/snippet-tests).
- Accessibility check: images have alt text, headings order correct.
- Update redirects and nav where needed (docs-site config file).
3) Post-publish monitoring
- Monitor search index errors (weekly).
- Track page load and 404 rates (SLO: 99.9% pages served).
- Spike in support tickets: label and route to DevEx for triage.
4) Emergency rollback
- If a publish introduces breaking docs: revert PR, rollback artifact, and post status update to #devex-ops.

Snippet & Example Validation
- CI jobs must run each code snippet with official SDK versions in matrix (latest-1, latest).
- Snippet failures create a blocking status on the docs PR and notify the author.

API Examples: canonical patterns
- Text generation (sync): show REST POST /v1/generate with body, headers, and sample 200 response.
- Chat (stateful): show turn-by-turn example including role/content and expected message format.
- Streaming: show Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket examples and client-side consumption pseudocode.
- Embeddings: include batching example (Python) and best practices for nearest-neighbor indexing.
- Function/Tool Calling: show function schema, call example, and recommended validation steps.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (top 12)
For each issue include: symptom, root cause, reproduction steps, canonical fix, mitigation, owner. Example entries:
1) Authentication failures: invalid API key or expired credential
- Symptom: 401 responses from SDKs
- Repro: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" ... with malformed key
- Fix: confirm key format, rotate API key in dashboard, update SDK environment variables to use REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Mitigation: SDKs should surface clear error messages and link to reset flow
- Owner: pkg-sdks
2) Streaming connections drop under load
- Symptom: intermittent SSE/WS disconnects for long-lived streams
- Root cause: idle connection timeouts on intermediate proxies or aggressive autoscaling on Dedicated pools
- Repro: start 100 concurrent streaming clients and watch disconnects after ~90s
- Fix: update proxy timeouts, enable ping keepalive, and increase stream idle threshold in gateway config
- Mitigation: add client retry/backoff sample in streaming quickstart
- Owner: eng-platform + eng-serving-runtime
3) Model mismatch / schema errors in function calling
- Symptom: 400s with validation errors when calling tools/functions
- Fix: ensure function schema is valid JSON Schema, include serialization helper in SDKs
- Owner: applied-ml-and-evals
4) High-cost token usage due to missing batching/cache
- Symptom: elevated per-token billing on high-throughput endpoints
- Fix: enable prefix caching and recommend batch endpoint usage in quickstarts; add quantization profiles in model onboarding
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime
(Include remaining top issues in the same format; full list is maintained in the support tracker.)

Publishing Checklist (pre-merge PR template)
1. Title and summary present
2. Author and owner_team set
3. Related pages & labels updated
4. Snippet tests passed (CI)
5. Staging URL provided and smoke tests green
6. Reviewers assigned and approvals obtained

Observability & Metrics for Docs
- Page SLOs: 99.5% search relevance, 99.9% page availability.
- Docs CI: 100% snippet pass rate on merge to main.
- Support reduction target: reduce repeat doc-related tickets by 40% YoY.

Support Handoff & Triage Process
1) Support engineer identifies doc-related ticket and labels it \"docs-action\".
2) Triage in weekly support-ops meeting; severity and owner assigned.
3) If urgent, create hotfix PR using doc-site ops emergency rollback flow.

Appendix A - Quickstart: Node.js streaming chat (copy/paste)
// Install: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async () => {
  const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'rw-chat-large-v1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello, summarize the last quarter.' }] });
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.delta);
  }
})();
Expected output: streaming deltas printed to stdout.

Appendix B - Example API request (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-text-large-v1","input":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'
Sample response: {\"id\":\"gen_123\",\"output\":\"Bonjour le monde\"} (200)

Appendix C - Template: Quickstart README skeleton
- Title
- Objective
- Prereqs
- Quickstart (1-file example)
- Tests and CI
- Deploy notes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Support & troubleshooting

Maintenance & Review Cadence
- Major guides: review every 6 months.
- Quickstarts: review every 3 months or on SDK release.
- Top support issues: review monthly in support-ops sync.

Related artifacts and links
- DevEx docs-site repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-docs (snippet-tests CI)
- SDK repos: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python, sdk-js, sdk-go
- Support tracker: internal ticket board (#support-docs)

Contact and escalation
- Primary: DevEx (devex@redwood.ai)
